newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won weaker at midday on intervention fear.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won weaker at midday on intervention fear.

text.p: The won weakened slightly by midday on Tuesday after a central bank official said the Bank of Korea (BOK) was considering buying dollars to stop the rise of the won, dealers said.
The BOK official, who declined to be identified, said it would be desirable for the local unit to move in line with other Asian currencies against the dollar.
The won opened at the day's high of 888.80 but fell to 890.60 after his comment. The won stood at 890.00 for the lunch break. Monday's close was 888.90.
